component.name: Baking Powder
component.summary: A compact DAW in black and white

description.p: Baking Powder is a compact digital audio workstation: one synthesizer, twelve effects, a chord palette and a grid, drawn in black and white.

Every track carries the Core, a polyphonic synthesizer with two oscillators (unison, FM and hard sync), fifteen colors of noise, four filter designs (state-variable, ladder, OTA and diode), amp and filter envelopes, a pitch envelope, analog drift, mono glide and a chord-order arpeggiator. Behind it sits a rack of up to twelve effects: Reverb, Delay, Distortion, Chorus, Phaser, Flanger, Compressor, EQ with a live spectrum analyzer, Volume LFO, Tape, Utility and Transient. Every parameter is a square you press and drag.

Pick a key and a scale, and the chord palette lays out the chords that belong to them: press one to hear it, drag it onto the grid to place it as a one-bar clip. Clips move by the beat, stretch, join and delete. Sixteen send buses, a master fader with peak meters and a clip indicator, a metronome, and a computer keyboard that plays like a piano.
Projects are plain JSON files. Undo runs a hundred steps deep. The app reopens exactly as you left it, in a light or dark theme with adjustable contrast. No account, no network, no audio input.

screenshot.caption: The main window: the header rail, track tiles, the grid, the Core and the effects rack

description.p: Recording: a RECORD button in the header records takes onto the selected track, drawn as they will print.
A piano roll for editing clips note by note, a ruler that places the playhead and paints the loop, and automation drawn as nodes on the track's lane.
WAV export of the song, rack and row presets saved and loaded as JSON, and an adjustable audio buffer in Settings.
The palette meters the sounding chord while playing, the header names the saved project, and the filters run faster.
